title: A.X K2 serving re-measurement protocol on 2 x ND96amsr A100 v4 (vLLM v0.23.0)
status: Pre-registration. The screening ran on GPUs (main 5dc653b; follow-ups: mp-multinode C4m, C8m, C16m at 6fe428d; PD retries at 2d104e4, b7760b0 and 50d51d9); results are in docs/report/SCREENING_2026-11-10.md. The rounds have not run. Round layouts (2026-11-10): A + B0 + D42 (the pre-registered selection) + C8m + D24 (added after the screening by the user's decision; deviations), in an FP8 and an NVFP4 round job per round (rounds.jobs); on 2026-11-11 the user chose the reinforced plan (accuracy on 1,000 items, the D2 control, W1real for the NVFP4 layouts; budget.user_budget). Before round 1, freeze aml/src/bench/ (this file, slo_suites.py, accuracy.py, protocol.sh, bench_stats.py, lb_proxy.py, node_tools.py, nixl_preflight.py) and docs/BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md in one commit; publish every run, including invalid and aborted runs.
assumptions: The SLO tiers are assumptions until the customer agrees them (or supplies its own) before round 1.

The common --max-model-len of 131072 must be at least the customer's longest input plus output; every round layout held it in the screening, and the round-1 capacity phases (cap-*) record each layout's KV-fitted maximum.
Prices change; pull the Azure retail prices again on the publication date.

deviations.what: C8m and D24 run in the rounds although the pre-registered selection rule (screen.selection) chose only B0 and D42
deviations.why: the user's decision after the screening report: A + B0 + D42 + C8 + D24, all throughput candidates (C8 = the mp-multinode C8m; the Ray C8 cannot start)
deviations.effect: their comparisons are labelled 'added after screening' in every analyze and report output (rounds.selection)

nvfp4.requires: NVFP4_SM80_PORT=1 (applied by apply_overlay.py at job start)

server.prefix_caching: on (the production default); every measured point starts idle, after POST /reset_prefix_cache, and fails its gate if more than 1% of the queried prompt tokens hit the cache
server.eager_fallback: forbidden: a comparison phase that does not start with CUDA graphs fails; it is never retried with --enforce-eager
server.transport: FP8 two-node phases need NCCL over InfiniBand: the phase fails when the IB probe did not choose IB or any communicator used NET/Socket
notes: --max-num-seqs and --max-num-batched-tokens are per engine; C2 (DP2) therefore has twice A's system-wide budget, which C2s halves.
--api-server-count 1 removes C2's default of two API servers; --async-scheduling and the CUDA graph mode pin what vLLM 0.23 otherwise chooses.

dp_ep_batch_rule.rule: A two-node FP8 DP x EP layout shares C2's total batch budget of 16,384 tokens: per engine 16,384 / DP (C2 8,192, C4 4,096, C8 2,048, C16 1,024). NVFP4: D8 1,024, D24 8,192. A sensitivity layout (C2s, C4s, ...) keeps its own definition: total 8,192 (A's), per engine 8,192 / DP.
dp_ep_batch_rule.reason: With all2all_backend allgather_reducescatter, vLLM 0.23 gathers every DP rank's tokens per MoE forward without chunking, so the profile run sizes the Marlin MoE workspace for M = DP x max_num_batched_tokens tokens (about 229,376 bytes per token in BF16). At 8,192 tokens per engine C8 would leave about 19K KV tokens per engine and C16 and D8 would run out of memory.

launchers.note: How a layout's server starts. Default: one vllm serve on node0 (Ray places a two-node layout's workers on node1; a phase with replicas starts a second server on node1 through the bench replica actor). A layout with "launcher": "mp-multinode" uses the launch below.

mp-multinode.description: vLLM's documented multi-node data parallelism without Ray (docs/serving/data_parallel_deployment.md:37-47 of v0.23.0): node0 serves the single API endpoint and DP ranks 0..L-1; node1 runs ranks L..DP-1 headless and connects to node0's address and RPC port
mp-multinode.api_only_note: Node1 gets every flag of node0 except these API-server flags, plus peer_args. --reasoning-parser stays on both nodes: vLLM 0.23 passes it to the engine (StructuredOutputsConfig and ReasoningConfig, vllm/engine/arg_utils.py:610, 2171-2177, 2441-2445). --headless rejects --api-server-count above 0 (vllm/entrypoints/cli/serve.py); node0 never gets --data-parallel-start-rank, which would switch it to hybrid load balancing.

placeholders.@head_ip: node0's address, the same value on both nodes

mp-multinode.order: node0 first, node1 within seconds after it (a remote engine waits about 5 minutes for the head's reply to its HELLO). Only node0's /health is awaited: the head answers once every DP engine of both nodes has connected. Node1's process is checked every minute, so the wait ends when it exits.
mp-multinode.relaunch: A length fallback stops and relaunches both nodes with -1; vLLM's KV-capacity error may appear in either node's log (node0's log, node1's log tail).
mp-multinode.stop: node1's process group (bench replica stop), then node0's session, every time; the clean-state checks cover both nodes

ray_dp_failure.measured: Screening at main 5dc653b: C4, C8 and C16 (Ray DP backend, two or more engines per node) failed about 70 s after start in RayWorkerProc.initialize_worker -> ncclCommInitRank with NCCL error 'invalid usage'. C2 (Ray DP, one engine per node) and D8, D24 (mp DP, several engines on one node) passed.
ray_dp_failure.inferred: Verified by elimination in NCCL 2.28.9: the only ncclInvalidUsage path of ncclCommInitRank left is the duplicate-GPU check (src/init.cc:903-907). Likely: the DP group is the first communicator joining two engines of one node, and both engines' workers bound the same GPUs because RayExecutorV2 rewrites CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES in running workers (vllm/v1/executor/ray_executor_v2.py:368-397). The exact trigger is unknown.
ray_dp_failure.consequence: The same topologies run as C4m, C8m and C16m with this launcher; the Ray variants and their failed results stay as they are.

PD.description: NVFP4 prefill/decode disaggregation over NixlConnector (experimental): a prefill server (D, kv_producer) on node0 and a decode server (D, kv_consumer) on node1 behind lb_proxy.py --prefill/--decode on node0
PD.diagnosis: Screening (main 5dc653b): scr-PD failed at start in register_kv_caches with NIXL_ERR_BACKEND, 'VRAM memory is detected as host by UCX'. PD rerun (main 2d104e4, measured): the NIXL preflight failed on both nodes with the job's environment and with UCX_MEMTYPE_CACHE=n, every registration including the zero-length control, although the loader cache had libcuda, libnvidia-ml and libcudart and libuct_cuda was mapped; the preflight's environment record shows UCX_TLS=tcp and UCX_NET_DEVICES=eth0 in the job environment. Neither the image nor this harness sets them, so the Azure ML job runtime injects them (inferred). UCX_TLS=tcp leaves out cuda_copy, so UCX types VRAM as host memory: the root cause. The image's nixl-cu12 1.2.0 bundles UCX 1.21.0 built with CUDA; no rebuild is needed. Second PD rerun (main b7760b0, measured): with UCX_TLS=all and UCX_NET_DEVICES=all the preflight passed on both nodes, both servers started (KV 233,152 tokens each), the decode server logged 'NIXL compatibility check passed' and the smoke request through the proxy succeeded; then the prefill server ran out of GPU memory in sample_tokens on the first parity request (prompt logprobs: tried to allocate 1.25 GiB with 1.06 GiB free; another process held 486 MiB on that GPU, which D without PD does not have). PD therefore runs with --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85 instead of the common 0.9; its KV capacity is reported as measured.
PD.preflight: Before the servers start, nixl_preflight.py registers VRAM through NIXL on node0 and node1 with each variant in order: the job's UCX environment, then UCX_TLS=all and UCX_NET_DEVICES=all (vLLM's docs/features/nixl_connector_usage.md recommends them), then those and UCX_MEMTYPE_CACHE=n; each run takes 120 s at most. Both servers get exactly the first variant that passes on both nodes; if none passes the phase records 'PD not possible here: NIXL preflight failed (<reason>)' and does not start. node0.<phase>.preflight records the job's UCX_* values per node and the chosen variant. UCX_TLS is never a restricted list (all, or the job's own value).
PD.debug_relaunch: When the preflight passed and the launch still fails with 'VRAM memory is detected as host', both servers relaunch once with VLLM_LOGGING_LEVEL=DEBUG; their 'Registering descs' lines and any zero-length descriptor go to node0.<phase>.failure, and the phase stops without suites.
PD.note: vLLM 0.23 deprecates kv_role kv_both for NixlConnector (docs/features/nixl_connector_usage.md); the proxy follows tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/toy_proxy_server.py of v0.23.0. NIXL moves the KV cache over UCX, not NCCL: node0's InfiniBand counters per point show where it went. Each server sets VLLM_NIXL_SIDE_CHANNEL_HOST to its own node address at start.

phase_templates.note: PHASE_PLAN tokens <kind>-<layout> for a layout without an explicit phase (round candidates chosen by the screening): slo- (slo-sensitivity for a sensitivity layout), cap-, dx1-, dx2- and scr-. Explicit phases win; experimental layouts get none. The tokens slo-round-fp8 and slo-round-nvfp4 expand into a round job's phases (rounds.jobs).

rounds.design: Each round is two jobs that may run at the same time (at most three ND96 nodes): the FP8 job on two nodes and the NVFP4 job on one node, so no NVFP4 layout leaves a second node idle. A job runs its reference -> its candidates in the round's order -> (round 2) the sensitivity runs -> its control -> (round 2) the capacity phases. A job's baseline of a round is the geometric mean of its reference and its control (A and A2, D and D2) for the metrics both launches measured.
rounds.layouts_rule: A round job compares its candidates with its reference: ROUND_LAYOUTS (comma-separated) or the job's frozen list. A candidate must be a layout of the job's checkpoint that fits its nodes and is neither the reference, its relaunch, a sensitivity nor an experimental layout. Odd rounds run the candidates in the listed order, even rounds in reverse (B0,C8m: round 1 B0 then C8m, round 2 C8m then B0). A ROUND_LAYOUTS that differs from the frozen list runs and is recorded as a deviation (protocol-plan.json). Rounds 4 and 5 run only if the extension rule fires.

selection.label: added after screening
selection.rule: screen.selection chose B0 (FP8) and D42 (NVFP4); the D x 2 decision passed
selection.decision: After the screening report (docs/report/SCREENING_2026-11-10.md) the user chose 'A + B0 + D42 + C8 + D24' (all throughput candidates, about 76 node-hours, about $980); C8 is the mp-multinode layout C8m because the Ray C8 cannot start

rounds.order: reference; candidates as listed in odd rounds, reversed in even rounds; (round 2) sensitivity runs; control; (round 2) cap-<reference> and cap-<candidate>
rounds.sensitivity: <X>s for every candidate X that has a sensitivity layout (C2s, C4s, C8s, C16s, C4ms, C8ms, C16ms): X's per-engine limits divided by its DP size, so its system-wide budget equals A's. Of the round layouts only C8m has one (C8ms, FP8 job, round 2); B0 and D42 run one engine and D24 (two engines) has no sensitivity layout
rounds.round_two: the sensitivity run and the capacity phases run in round 2, not round 1 as the integrated review planned: the round-1 jobs carry the 1,000-item accuracy run and must stay under the 12-hour job limit (decided 2026-11-11, before the freeze)
rounds.capacity: cap-<reference> and cap-<X> for every candidate X of the job
rounds.soak_rates: SOAK_RATES=<rates key>=<req/s>,...: 0.8 x the mean lambda*(W1, standard SLO) of each layout over the valid rounds 1 and 2 of its job, printed by bench_stats.py analyze (soak_rates); a lambda* known only as a bound uses 0.8 x that bound
rounds.validity: per round job: it counts only if every measuring suite of its reference, candidates and control reported, none aborted and every planned point has a valid attempt (the soak included in round 3); a comparison uses the rounds in which every job it involves is valid
rounds.allocations: Every round is a new pair of jobs. The FP8 job of round 3 must run on a different node pair from rounds 1 and 2 (compare the hashed host names); rounds 1 and 2 may share one. A preempted or failed job is resubmitted whole, and only one package per round and job is analyzed.

R.description: Part R: replay of the published 1K/8K/32K x concurrency 1 and 32 matrix

S1.description: W1 lengths at fixed concurrency (closed loop)

W1real.description: W1 lengths with real Korean and English text (aml/src/bench/parity_corpus.json windows, or the customer's JSONL)
W1real.note: every round layout runs it with its full suites: the FP8 phases by checkpoint (A, B0, C8m) and the NVFP4 round layouts by name (D, D42, D24; the user's decision of 2026-11-11); real-text expert routing can differ from random tokens in the EP layouts C8m and D24

soak.description: W1 at 0.8 x lambda* of the standard SLO for 45 minutes (soak round only)

warmup.description: discarded: one 32-request burst per input length, 64 output tokens, then a cache reset

rate_grids.status: pre-registered from the screening (docs/report/SCREENING_2026-11-10.md) and fixed for every round by the freeze commit
rate_grids.lookup: a phase looks its grid up under its rates key (its own layout name; A2, D2 and the sensitivity layouts use their base layout's, dx2-D uses Dx2): SLO_RATES_<key> (an override, reported as a deviation) > grids.<key> > the phase's rate set > the workload's rates

rule.W1: every round layout met the standard SLO with goodput 1.0 at 0.6 req/s (scr-* W1 point), D missed it at 1.0 req/s (goodput 0.55, scr-Dx1) and every other round layout had a higher W1 TPOT p90 at 0.6 req/s than D (68-86 ms against 62 ms), so every lambda* is expected between 0.6 and 1.0 req/s; the grid keeps both measured rates, adds their geometric mean (0.78) and 0.45 = 0.75 x 0.6 for the strict tier (D's strict lambda* lay between 0.25 and 0.6)
rule.W2: no layout ran W2 in the screening; lambda*(W2) is estimated as 0.5 / P, P = the 8K prefill time at concurrency 1 (R/isl8192-c1 TTFT p50), i.e. prefill busy half the time; the grid runs geometrically from 0.6 x the lowest estimate to 1.4 x the highest
rule.shared: one grid per workload for every round layout keeps the per-point metrics (W1/p1, ...) comparable across layouts and jobs; it is what next_grid's rule (0.6 x to 1.4 x lambda*, shared when one grid brackets every layout) gives for these estimates
rule.Dx2: twice D's grid, so each replica of dx2-D sees dx1-D's per-server load
rule.unbracketed: a lambda* outside its grid is reported as a bound and its comparisons are inconclusive; the grids stay fixed in every round
rule.strict: the strict tier is a secondary metric. When the lowest W1 rate (0.45 req/s) already misses the strict SLO, strict lambda* is reported as a bound below the grid (lambda* < 0.45 req/s); expected at least for C8m and D42 (strict goodput at 0.6 req/s in the screening: 0.00 and 0.028) and possibly for other DP x EP and PP layouts. No rate is added for it

sampling.never: --num-warmups (it resends prompt 0, which then hits the prefix cache)

slo.assumption: ASSUMPTION: agree these tiers (or the customer's own) before round 1.
slo.definition: lambda* = the highest arrival rate at which at least 90% of the steady-state requests (by start time) meet both the TTFT and the TPOT limit; failed requests count as misses

seeds.point: index of the point in its workload's full list (rate grid or Part R list), so subsets keep their seeds
seeds.rerun: an invalid point is rerun once with the same seed (common random numbers) after a cache reset
seeds.rate_order_formula: 1000000*ROUND + 10000*WORKLOAD + 99 seeds a shuffle of the grid indices; the same order for every layout

p1.one_at_a_time: one 2,048-token document per request, sent one after another, so a prefill chunk never holds more than 2,048 tokens of prompt logprobs (about 1.25 GiB of fp32 log-softmax)

p3.suite: paritylong, the last suite of a phase
p3.compare: against the job's reference launch: index of the first differing generated token, position-wise token agreement, and mean |delta logprob| of the chosen tokens before the first difference; the control's values (A2, D2) are the floor
p3.suspect: suspect when the continuations of both long documents differ from the reference's before token 4: reported per launch and investigated before the results are used; it does not change the round's validity
p3.why_not_prompt_logprobs: vLLM 0.23 computes prompt logprobs over a whole prefill chunk (GPUModelRunner._get_prompt_logprobs_dict: compute_logits of every scheduled prompt token, then Sampler.compute_logprobs = log_softmax in float32), so a 32K document in 8,192-token chunks needs about 8,192 x 163,840 x 4 B = 5.0 GiB plus the bf16 logits; the screening left about 1 GiB free at 0.9 (the PD retry 2 prefill server ran out of memory asking 1.25 GiB for a 2,048-token chunk)
p3.coverage: 64 generated tokens at positions beyond 32,768, where the DSA indexer chooses 2,048 of 32K positions for every token: weaker than teacher-forced logprobs of every position, but within the memory the server has

parity.reference: slo-<reference> of the same round job: slo-A in the FP8 job, slo-D in the NVFP4 job

acceptance.applies: every candidate and sensitivity run of a round job against its reference, with the job's control as the floor (FP8: A2 vs A; NVFP4: D2 vs D)
acceptance.early_divergence: a first difference before token 16 on more than 2 of the 32 greedy prompts means the layout is misconfigured

parity.nvfp4: NVFP4 and FP8 run in different jobs, so no token-level parity of D against A is computed; quality is the accuracy section's paired comparison (KoBALT 700 + CLIcK 300, McNemar, non-inferiority margin -3 points)

accuracy.status: pre-registered NVFP4-against-FP8 accuracy subset: the quality prerequisite of the NVFP4 layouts

kobalt.source: aml/src/evals.py KOBALT: snunlp/KoBALT-700 at its pinned revision, sha256-checked

click.source: aml/src/evals.py CLICK: EunsuKim/CLIcK at its pinned revision, 26 files checked by git blob id

accuracy.selection: evals.py sample(): the n items with the smallest sha256('<seed>|sample|<dataset>|<key>'), kept in the dataset's order (all 700 KoBALT items, 300 of the 1,995 CLIcK items); the same items on both servers

request.order: both datasets shuffled together by sha256('<seed>|order|<dataset>|<key>')

accuracy.scoring: the final answer after the reasoning (evals.final_answer), scored as evals.py does; a reply that reaches max_tokens counts as wrong (hit_limit)

comparison.difference: d = accuracy(NVFP4) - accuracy(FP8) over the items both servers scored
comparison.interval: two-sided 95% Wald interval of a paired difference: d +- 1.96 x sqrt(b + c - (c - b)^2 / n) / n, with b = FP8 right and NVFP4 wrong, c = the reverse
comparison.test: exact two-sided McNemar test (binomial test of the b + c discordant items with p = 1/2)

decision.non-inferior: the lower bound of the interval is above the margin
decision.inferior: the upper bound is below the margin

comparison.primary: pooled over both datasets (1,000 items); each dataset alone is secondary
comparison.incomplete: when at least 99% of the items were scored on both servers the decision is complete; when fewer but at least 800 items were (for example because the 3 h cap fired; the unfinished items are the slowest replies) the same decision rule is applied to those items and reported as partial coverage; below 800 the result is reported without a decision

accuracy.power_note: ESTIMATE (normal approximation, no true difference): the chance of a non-inferior result at 10% discordant items is about 56% with 500 items and about 85% with 1,000; with 1,000 items about 99% at 5%, 69% at 15% and 56% at 20% discordance. Greedy reasoning chains can disagree on 10-20% of the items
accuracy.failure: a download or client failure fails only the accuracy suite (recorded in <phase>.accuracy.json); the phase's other suites and the round's validity do not depend on it
accuracy.cost: about 2 hours per server (estimate: 700 x 3,478 + 300 x 1,038 completion tokens, the October averages, at about 400 tok/s with 32 in flight); the suite stops at 3 hours

gates.preemptions: a point with preemptions is marked capacity-bound, not invalid
gates.kv_bound: a point whose peak KV usage on any engine is >= 0.95, or whose closed-loop peak of running requests stays below its concurrency, is marked KV-bound and kept out of speed decisions

throttle.note: Invalid: HW slowdown (0x8), SW thermal (0x20), HW thermal (0x40), HW power brake (0x80). SW power cap (0x4) is the normal operating limit of a loaded A100 and is reported per point, not invalidating; 02-bench-audit c.5 proposed idle-only.

gates.round: a round counts only if every planned point of every planned phase has a valid attempt; never use a round in part

statistics.steady_state: requests whose start time falls in the workload window; output tok/s counts the per-token timestamps (start + TTFT + cumulative ITL) inside the window

bootstrap.method: moving blocks of consecutive requests spanning 30 s of arrivals

lambda_star.interpolation: linear between the last grid rate that meets the threshold and the next one
lambda_star.bound: outside its grid lambda* is a bound: below the grid when the lowest rate misses the threshold, above the grid when the highest rate still meets it

statistics.next_grid: information only: analyze prints four rates from 0.6 x to 1.4 x lambda* (geometric) per workload, shared when one grid brackets every layout; the rounds keep the frozen rate_grids

decision_rules.comparison: for metric M and round k, r_k = ln(M_X,k / M_base,k); M_base,k = sqrt(M_A,k x M_A2,k) when A2 measured M, else M_A,k; report exp(mean r) and exp(mean +- t_975(n-1) x sd / sqrt(n)) plus the min and max over rounds
better: the 95% CI of the ratio excludes 1
decision_rules.delta_min: max(ln 1.05, 2 x max_k |ln(A2_k / A_k)|) of the same metric; for metrics A2 did not measure, the largest such value over the metrics it did measure. Comparisons inside the NVFP4 job use its own control (D2); a job without a control would borrow the FP8 job's A/A2 values
decision_rules.cross_job: an NVFP4 layout against A compares two jobs of the same round (other nodes, the same seeds and grids); it is labelled cross-job, A's baseline is drift-corrected with A2 as above, and the rounds used are those in which both jobs are valid
decision_rules.equivalent: the whole 95% CI of the ratio lies in [0.95, 1.05]

extend.rule: add rounds (up to 5) when the SD over rounds of ln(A2/A) exceeds 2% for any overlapping primary metric or a primary metric's 95% CI half-width exceeds 5% in a comparison against A or D; a job extends when a reason involves it (a cross-job comparison involves both jobs)

decision_rules.a2_limitation: A2 runs start-up, warm-up, Part R and two W1 rates only, so drift correction applies to those metrics; lambda*, W2 and cost use A alone
ranking: cost per 1M output tokens at lambda*

prices_usd_per_node_hour.region: uksouth, Linux, Standard_ND96amsr_A100_v4 (Azure retail prices as recorded in evidence/a100-nvfp4-single-node.json)
prices_usd_per_node_hour.note: Low-priority capacity has been billed at the Spot rate since 2026-03-31; the older 8.19 low-priority rate no longer applies. Refresh every price before publishing.

dx2.pass: lambda*(Dx2) >= 1.9 x lambda*(Dx1) for W1 and W2 at the standard SLO
dx2.job: aml/jobs/slo-nvfp4-2replica-nd96.yml, once, with round-1 seeds; dx1-D runs on D's grid and dx2-D on twice that grid (rate_grids)

proxy.policy: least outstanding requests, ties in round-robin order

budget.status: ESTIMATES (not measured): the screening's phase and job durations (docs/report/SCREENING_2026-11-10.md section 7) scaled to the round suites

user_budget.decided: 2026-11-11: the reinforced plan (accuracy on 1,000 items, the D2 control, W1real for the NVFP4 round layouts); the round layouts on 2026-11-10

budget.assumptions: minutes per phase: start 5-8 (measured), parity 3-7, warm-up 2, Part R 21-24 in round 1 and 14-17 later, slo 77 (S1 10, four W1 rates 28, four W2 rates 34, overload drains 5), realtext 17, P3 1, soak 47, accuracy 120, stop and package 1.5; A2 and D2 run W1 points 1-2 (15); cap 9; job setup 28 (FP8), 21 (NVFP4), 12 (D x 2)
not_included: rounds 4 and 5 when the extension rule fires: about 22 node-hours each

pairs.name: A1: indexer grid scales with max_model_len
DCP: KV capacity and speed of TP16 with DCP 2

diagnostics.dcp_rule: DCP counts as supported only if diag-B0dcp starts, its KV tokens clearly exceed diag-B0's, the DCP group lines appear, parity against diag-A holds and the short load completes

screen.description: Screening before the rounds: one launch of every A100-feasible layout records start facts, short parity against the job's first launch, Part R and Poisson W1; every step and every phase fails softly (recorded, the job goes on)
screen.seeds: ROUND 0 of the seed formula (10000*WORKLOAD + 100*POINT): the same prompts for every layout, apart from every round
screen.order: Each job runs its reference first and the layouts expected to fail or to relaunch with -1 last (C16 and B0dcp in the FP8 job, C16m in the FP8 DP job, D8 in the NVFP4 job, PD in the two-node job), so a node they leave dirty cannot spoil a healthy phase.
screen.reference_rule: parity reference = the job's first launch: scr-A (both FP8 jobs), scr-D (NVFP4 job), scr-Dx1 (two-node NVFP4 job), scr-Dref (the PD rerun job)
screen.steps_option: a phase's options.screen.steps runs a subset of the steps: scr-Dref (D on node0) records start facts and parity only, the light parity reference of the PD rerun
screen.facts: seconds to healthy, the served max_model_len (/v1/models), KV tokens per engine (vllm:cache_config_info and every 'GPU KV cache size' log line), the requested and fitted length after a length fallback

parity.note: Loose on purpose: it catches a broken or misconfigured layout, not small numeric differences; the rounds apply the A2-based acceptance. Through PD, P1 (prompt_logprobs) reaches the prefill server alone; P2 runs the whole prefill -> KV transfer -> decode path.

partr.points: every Part R point at the published lengths (1,024 output tokens)
partr.capacity_note: 32 requests of 32K tokens with 64 output tokens record running requests, KV usage and preemptions only (a capacity point, never a speed number)

w1.note: W1 point p1 at 0.6 req/s (the grid's second rate): 360 s of arrivals, steady window 60-360 s

ladders.use: scr-Dx1 runs the W1 ladder, scr-Dx2 and scr-PD the dx2 ladder, instead of the single W1 point

screen.length_fallback: A screening server that cannot hold the common --max-model-len (vLLM: 'larger than the available KV cache memory') is relaunched once with -1; the requested and fitted lengths are recorded and the layout cannot join the rounds

selection.rule: A always. FP8: the eligible layout other than A with the highest R/isl8192-c32 output tok/s. NVFP4: the eligible one-node layout (D included) with the highest R/isl8192-c32 output tok/s. D x 2: when lambda*(W1, standard SLO) of scr-Dx2 >= 1.9 x that of scr-Dx1. Exact ties go to the layout listed first. A KV-bound or capacity-bound flag at the ranking point is reported next to the score with the peak KV usage and the peak of running requests; it never excludes a layout.
eligible: the phase passed (healthy start, effective-config and NCCL gates, the screen completed)
it held the common --max-model-len (no length fallback)
its short parity passed against the job's reference
the ranking point is valid (a KV-bound or capacity-bound flag there is reported, not excluded)
each listed c1 TPOT is at most tpot_max_ratio x the reference's
selection.same_job_reference: A candidate's reference (short parity and c1 TPOT) is the reference launch of its own job. A phase found in more than one package (scr-A of both FP8 jobs) is reported once per job, the later ones as <phase>@<job>, and every instance of a candidate phase competes.
selection.kv_bound_note: R/isl8192-c32 holds 32 x 9,216 = 294,912 tokens. D, E and Err (about 232K-254K KV tokens) and B0 (about 310K; peak KV usage 0.953 in the October run) are always KV-bound there, so the flag cannot exclude a layout or D, E and Err could never be chosen.

dx2.unbracketed: a lambda* outside its ladder is a bound; when the bounds cannot decide, the D x 2 job (slo-nvfp4-2replica-nd96.yml) decides with full grids

selection.pd: experimental: reported (lambda*, parity, preflight, failures, InfiniBand bytes), never selected in this protocol version. The PD rerun job has no Dx1 or Dx2: PD's pairs then take them from the earlier two-node job and are labelled cross-job.
selection.output: ROUND_LAYOUTS=<FP8 choice>,<NVFP4 choice>; the FP8 choice is a candidate of the FP8 round job and the NVFP4 choice of the NVFP4 round job (rounds.jobs); round 1 adds <X>s when the FP8 choice has a sensitivity layout

estimates.status: ESTIMATES, not measurements: model shape plus the evidence below; the screening records the real weights, KV tokens and fitted lengths
estimates.formula: weights per GPU = (routed experts / EP + shared experts (whole on every rank when sequence-parallel MoE applies: DP > 1, TP > 1, EP; whole anyway at TP1) + TP-sharded non-expert / TP + replicated non-expert) x (layers of the worst pipeline stage / 61); KV tokens per engine = (0.9 x 80 GiB - weights - other) / (1,284 B x layers per GPU)
estimates.kv_bytes_note: bf16 MLA latent 1,152 B + DSA indexer key 132 B, replicated on every TP rank; the ported TRITON_MLA_SPARSE backend has no FP8 KV cache (auto/fp16/bf16 only)

other_gib.note: activations, CUDA graphs and buffers, from the evidence: TP/PP about 3 (A), NVFP4 TP8 about 6.6 (D); DP x EP layouts add the Marlin MoE workspace of M = DP x max_num_batched_tokens tokens (server.dp_ep_batch_rule)

estimates.source: C4, C8, C16, D8, D24 and B0dcp: launch check of the screening layouts against the vLLM v0.23.0 source, at the per-engine batch sizes of server.dp_ep_batch_rule

reporting.primary: Every protocol job packages its own results (bench_stats.py package --report) after each phase and on exit, and reports them through report.py as chunked MLflow tags: the parts slo.package.<launch> (that launch's points) first, then slo.package (everything but the points, with each part's launch). Workspace storage is private and the workspace has no CPU cluster, so this in-job path is primary; collect-slo-outputs.yml is a fallback.
reporting.missing_part: a part that never arrived invalidates only the launch it holds
reporting.best_effort: bounded with timeout, never changes the job's exit status
